INSTITUCIONES_COLABORADORAS: Universidad Nacional de Colombia
RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: ABSTRACT Orchidaceae is one of the largest plant families and includes species of major ornamental, economic, and ecological importance. Despite this diversity, the viruses associated with orchids remain poorly characterized. The growing availability of high-throughput sequencing data offers new opportunities to explore plant virus diversity across broad taxonomic scales. Here, we conducted a large-scale meta-analysis of orchid-associated viruses by reanalyzing 2,789 publicly available RNA-seq data sets representing 41 genera across 18 subtribes and five subfamilies. We identified sequences corresponding to 163 viruses, including 13 new associations with orchids. Notably, 117 sequences likely represent putative novel species, including tentative new genera within the families Benyviridae , Betaflexiviridae , Phenuiviridae , and Tymoviridae . This analysis also reveals patterns of virus co-occurrence within the orchid virome and uncovers links between viral taxa and orchid life forms. Overall, these findings greatly broaden the known diversity of orchid-associated viruses and offer a comprehensive global framework for understanding their composition, ecological interactions, and potential scope. IMPORTANCE Orchids are among the most diverse plant families, yet little is known about the viruses associated with them. Plant viruses pose significant risks to agriculture and may also threaten orchid conservation, particularly when infected plant material is moved through trade or cultivation. A comprehensive understanding of the orchid virome is therefore essential for improving virus detection, managing diseases, and producing virus-free planting material. In this study, we used large-scale analysis of publicly available RNA-seq data to identify viral sequences associated with orchid-derived transcriptomic data sets and to characterize the diversity of orchid-associated viruses. Our results substantially expand the catalog of viruses associated with Orchidaceae, revealing numerous previously undescribed viruses and candidate virus-orchid associations. By providing a global perspective on the Orchidaceae virome, this work highlights the power of data mining approaches for virus discovery and establishes a foundation for future studies on plant virus ecology, evolution, and surveillance.

RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: Accurate geospatial data is essential for monitoring land-use change and supporting sustainable territorial management. This study evaluates five image fusion techniques – injection, average interpolation, ratio component substitution, Bayesian, and local mean variance matching – to integrate Sentinel-2 (10 m and 20 m) with PlanetScope (3.1 m) imagery for land use/land cover (LULC) mapping in two Colombian watersheds characterized by high environmental and social complexity. Unlike prior studies, we propose a systematic band-pairing framework based on spectral linear regression that integrates SWIR-1 and SWIR-2 bands to produce super-resolution outputs. The fused datasets were assessed using standard fusion quality metrics and thematic accuracy indicators. Results show that the regression-based pairing improves fusion consistency, while the Bayesian method yields the highest classification accuracy, particularly in heterogeneous landscapes. This work advances current fusion practices by offering a transparent, reproducible methodology for integrating multiscale satellite data, overcoming spectral mismatches in SWIR bands, and enabling fine-scale LULC monitoring. The proposed approach offers a practical, scalable alternative to black-box models, yielding more accurate and timely spatial information for sustainable land management and policy development.

AUTORES: Ashraf A. Isayed; Zain González-Rosas; Juan Maria Menendez-Aguado; Óscar Jaime Restrepo Baena; Hatem Jemmali
INSTITUCIONES_COLABORADORAS: Universidad de Oviedo, Universidad Nacional de Colombia, Manouba University
RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: This study analyses the impact of mining activities on water scarcity in two contrasting mining regions: Zaragoza, Colombia, and Qabatiya, Palestine. Despite significant climatic and hydrological differences, both regions face substantial pressures on water resources and governance systems caused by mining. To assess these pressures on water security, the Water Poverty Index (WPI) has gained the attention as a holistic tool; however, its application in regions dominated by informal extractive economies presents a critical scientific gap; standard WPI methodologies rely heavily on low-resolution, macro-level secondary data, which inherently smooths out localized socio-environmental crises and creates a “compensation bias” in which temporary economic inflows mask severe ecological degradation. Furthermore, conventional frameworks fail to capture the dynamics of informal hydro-social governance, territorial conflicts, and non-conventional pollutants that characterize data-scarce extraction zones. To address this gap, this study applied four versions of the Water Poverty Index (WPI), Conventional, classic-inclusive, geometric, and arithmetic, to evaluate longitudinal changes between 2010 and 2025 under counterfactual baselines versus active extraction scenarios. The framework assessed six components: Resources, Access, Capacity, Use, Environment, and Cohesion, integrating both quantitative indicators and qualitative evidence. Results revealed that mining consistently reduced WPI performance in both localities, particularly within the Environment, Use, and Cohesion dimensions. Zaragoza exhibited a generalized decline across all WPI versions due to mercury contamination, institutional fragility, and social fragmentation associated with informal alluvial gold mining. At the same time, Qabatiya saw moderate infrastructure improvements, offset by groundwater depletion and environmental degradation from stone quarrying. The iWPI versions demonstrated superior sensitivity in capturing governance and socio-environmental degradation. The study concludes that water poverty in mining regions is multidimensional and driven by interconnected environmental, institutional, economic, and social pressures (as measured by the WPI), rather than by physical water scarcity alone.

AUTORES: Natalia C Gonzalez-Jimenez; María C. Lozano; Yolima Baena
INSTITUCIONES_COLABORADORAS: Universidad Nacional de Colombia, Fundación Universitaria del Área Andina
RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: Introduction Proparacaine hydrochloride is a topical ocular anesthetic widely used in diagnostic procedures. Although generally safe when properly administered, repeated or unsupervised use has been associated with clinically relevant corneal injury. In contexts where access to topical anesthetics is insufficiently controlled, misuse may result in cumulative epithelial damage and vision-threatening complications. Despite clinical reports and experimental evidence of corneal toxicity, quantitative data linking exposure conditions to structural corneal damage under controlled ex vivo settings remain limited, particularly regarding dose-injury relationships at the tissue level.Methods Porcine corneas were mounted in Franz diffusion cells to quantify permeation by UV–Vis spectrophotometry and evaluate corneal histopathological changes. Both pure proparacaine and the commercial 0.5% proparacaine hydrochloride ophthalmic solution (Alcaine®, Alcon) were assessed under therapeutic (2.25 mg/mL), abuse (4.5 mg/mL), and infinite-dose (53.152 mg/mL) conditions. Negative (phosphate-buffered saline) and positive (99.5% ethanol) controls were included for histopathological assessment. ANOVA was applied to permeation data, and histopathological scores were analyzed using non-parametric tests.Results Proparacaine showed low permeability (9.33 × 10−7 cm/s), with only a small fraction of the applied dose permeating across the cornea during the experimental period. Permeation increased in a concentration- and time-dependent manner. High-dose and infinite-dose exposure conditions resulted in marked epithelial damage, including spongiosis, chromatin condensation, and desquamation, with severity comparable to that induced by ethanol used as a positive control. Differences between formulations were primarily driven by concentration rather than formulation composition, and a correlation was observed between cumulative permeation and the extent of epithelial injury.Conclusion Proparacaine demonstrates dose-dependent permeation and histopathological changes, emphasizing the risks associated with misuse. The ex vivo model provides relevant and ethically aligned evidence to support ocular hazard assessment through the characterizing of histopathological changes.

RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: Los efluentes procedentes de la parbolización del arroz contienen compuestos no biodegradables que resultan tóxicos para los ecosistemas acuáticos. En este estudio, se utilizó un catalizador de Fe altamente disperso sobre sílice obtenida de cascarilla de arroz (5Fe@SiO2) para la reacción de oxidación del fenol presente en aguas residuales de la parbolización del arroz. La reacción se hizo a 25 °C y a presión atmosférica. El catalizador alcanzó una reducción de la demanda química de oxígeno (DQO) del 67±3 %, una mineralización del 68,4±2,2 % y una conversión de fenol del 81,4±2 % después de 36 horas. El rendimiento del catalizador en la oxidación de fenol demuestra el potencial de aplicación del material en el tratamiento de aguas residuales. Dichos sistemas constituyen una estrategia para la conservación de los recursos naturales y la preservación de la biodiversidad en Colombia. Este estudio constituye una contribución a la estrategia de transición hacia la economía circular.

AUTORES: Eduardo José Campechano Escalona; Isabel Cristina Díaz de Campechano; Gioconda Carmela Bellomo Montalvo; Luis Enrique Ibarra Morales; Giovanni Pérez Ortega; Manuel José Peñalver-Higuera

RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: Este artículo aborda el papel que desarrolla la Sociedad civil organizada (SCO) de Perú, México y Colombia para la implementación de la Agenda 2030. El objetivo fue analizar bajo un enfoque comparativo los aportes, área de acción y desafíos que existen en estos países a partir de las 5P. El estudio responde al paradigma interpretativo con un enfoque cualitativo para realizar un análisis hermenéutico del contenido de los portales de las ONG de Colombia, México y Perú haciendo uso del Atlas TI. Utilizando una matriz de contenido para la recolección de los datos que se declararon en la misión y visión de cada una de las iniciativas analizadas, se obtuvieron una serie de categorías y subcategorías que permitieron reconstruir nubes de palabras y un diagrama Sankey a partir de las 5P de la Agenda 2030. Estos resultados destacan la importancia de fortalecer desde las universidades las capacidades de la SCO para promover la participación ciudadana y fomentar la colaboración entre los diferentes actores involucrados. Entre las consideraciones finales se resalta el rol de las Instituciones de Educación Superior como actores claves para configurar un modelo de gobernanza con planes de acción que se adapten a las realidades de cada país, con el fin de maximizar el impacto de la SCO en la consecución de la Agenda 2030.

AUTORES: Jorge Ramirez Osorio
INSTITUCIONES_COLABORADORAS: Universidad Nacional de Colombia
RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: We consider stochastic Lotka-Volterra systems $dX=\mathrm{Diag}(X)(α+AX)dt+\mathrm{Diag}(X)ΓdB$ with nondegenerate noise and a Volterra-Lyapunov stable interaction matrix $A$, that is, $DA+A^\top D\prec 0$ for some positive diagonal matrix $D$. This class covers every self-limited predator-prey food web that is conservative in the sense of Volterra, in particular every such web whose interaction graph is a forest. We give a necessary and sufficient condition for invariant coexistence: the process has an invariant probability measure on $(0,\infty)^n$, that is, a stationary distribution under which all species have positive densities, if and only if $m=-A^{-1}β$ is positive, where $β=α-\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{diag}(ΓΓ^\top)$ is the vector of noise-corrected growth rates. This measure is then unique and ergodic, has mean $m$, and attracts every interior initial condition exponentially fast in total variation. Thus environmental noise affects coexistence only through the Itô shift $α\mapstoβ$, and the criterion is the exact counterpart of the feasibility criterion for the deterministic system $\dot x=\mathrm{Diag}(x)(β+Ax)$. Both directions rest on the fact that, for Lotka-Volterra systems, invasion rates are affine in the mean of the underlying measure. Necessity follows from an exact formula for the means of invariant measures supported on faces of the orthant. Sufficiency follows from the persistence theorem of Hening and Nguyen, for which the explicit weights $Dm$ give a stochastic counterpart of Hofbauer's average Lyapunov function, so that no enumeration of the invariant measures on the boundary is required. Applied to subcommunities, the result also characterizes every stationary regime in which some species are absent.

RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: Abstract Synthetic-based plasticizers are often used in the masonry industry to improve the rheological and mechanical properties of mortar, but these systems are neither sustainable nor eco-friendly. In this study, several copolymers were prepared that contain grafted β-cyclodextrin (βCD) and its modified forms (HprβCD, FβCD, SucβCD, and CarβCD) were grafted onto methoxy polyethylene glycol (MPEG) and were evaluated as hybrid bio-based plasticizing admixtures for cement mortar. The grafted copolymers were characterized by IR/1H NMR spectroscopy, powder XRD, TGA, and DSC. Their performance as admixtures were evaluated based on flowability, consistency, rheological parameters, and mechanical properties of mortar in fresh and hardened states. Spectral (27Al and 29Si NMR, XRD) measurements of the cementitious samples provided insight on the intermolecular interactions of the mortar components. At low concentrations, 1.0 wt %, the copolymers were effective plasticizers, increasing the mortar fluidity in comparison to the control sample without admixtures. At a 0.30: 1 water-to-cement ratio, the water reduction capacity was up to 20%, keeping the mortar flow within an appropriate range. Besides, hydration-related behavior was indirectly assessed through strength development and spectroscopic analyses. The mortar sample with HprβCD-MPEG had a higher compressive strength when the admixture concentration was changed from 1% (31 MPa) to 2% (40 MPa) showing the capacity of the copolymer as a strength enhancer. The copolymers CarβCD-MPEG (35 MPa) and FβCD-MPEG (42 MPa) also reached the compressive strength typical for a 28 day mortar sample, whereas a lower value was noted for the 7 day control (30 MPa). Relative to commercial superplasticizers, the graft copolymers showed high potential as suitable alternatives for conventional fully non-renewable admixtures.

RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: Abstract Aim Aortic stenosis (AS) is a common condition with exponential increases in incidence in aging populations. Perivascular adipose tissue (PVAT) forms the outer layer of the aortic wall and has – especially in the thoracic area – characteristics of thermogenic adipose tissue, which dissipates energy and releases endocrine factors. Here, we set out to investigate the role of thermogenic PVAT in AS. Methods and results We studied the role of (PVAT) in the development of AS in a murine model of AS. To specifically delineate the role of PVAT activity in AS, we used a pharmacological β3-adrenergic agonist as well as cold exposure in combination with a genetic mouse model with deficient PVAT development. To investigate the role of thermogenic adipose tissue in human AS, we used 18 F-FDG PET-CT imaging. We found that pharmacological activation of thermogenic adipose tissue resulted in an improvement of AS, but not in mice genetically deficient in PVAT. Similarly, PVAT was found to be protective against AS during physiological stimulation of PVAT using cold exposure. Mechanistically, PVAT activation resulted in enhanced aortic distensibility and cellular remodeling of the aortic wall, possibly via release of polyunsaturated fatty acids and oxylipins from perivascular adipocytes. Finally, analysis of thermogenic fat activity in humans revealed that mediastinal thermogenic fat activity correlated negatively with diagnostic criteria of AS severity, suggesting an important role for PVAT activity in human AS. Conclusion Our data indicate that PVAT activation reduces aortic stenosis and supports aortic remodeling to improve ascending aorta hemodynamics. PVAT activation might be a novel therapeutic target to ameliorate AS progression. Translational perspective Currently, there are no effective strategies for treating AS other than valve replacement. Since the molecular mechanisms underlying the disease progression remain unclear, there are no pharmacological agents approved for either treatment or prevention of this disease. Furthermore, AS development cannot currently be predicted and is often only diagnosed when patients develop symptoms, which may be 10-20 years after disease onset. Therefore, identifying novel mechanisms that improve aortic valve function and prevent AS is of high medical need. This study identifies activation of PVAT-dependent aortic remodeling as a potential new therapeutic approach to improve or prevent AS.

RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: To advance the progress of membrane materials and process development, accurate prediction of membrane performance has to be efficiently optimized. Such optimization is challenging when sustainable materials such as hydrophilic biopolymers from renewable resources are used on mixed matrix-membrane (MMM) fabrication. In this work, we systematically developed a hybrid model architecture using a delta model design pattern to enhance the prediction of the permeability of chitosan-based MMM for CO 2 /N 2 separation and gain insight in the design of new sustainable membrane separation processes. The parametric model baseline is focused on the modified Maxwell equation including temperature dependence, involving the estimation of two interpretable parameters: void thickness (i.e. the interaction between the components of the membrane matrix) and the rigidification of the dispersed phase in the continuous matrix, with increasing level of complexity. The predictions of MMM using phenomenological modified Maxwell models are confirmed locally dependent with high uncertainty levels, meaning a high correlation between the optimized parameters. A sequential combination of global and local optimization methods, yielded the best parametric model performance, reducing error by up to an order of magnitude. Then, a multilayer perceptron neural network (MLPNN) is trained using the output error of the parametric model and the introduction of additional experimental input variables. The hybrid model significantly improves the accuracy of gas permeability prediction and the empirical interpretability agrees with the Mutual Information (MI) predictions. This way, this approach can be used to direct the development of phenomenological models to describe the transport through novel MMM.

RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: This text approaches making, care, and correspondence as vital, relational, and situated practices that bring together manual work, the creation of environments, the sustaining of life, and attentiveness to the human and more-than-human. Rather than examining these concepts separately, it considers them together through concrete experiences of research, teaching, writing, and creative practice. The discussion draws on three experiences undertaken at different times and scales. The first comes from the pedagogical work of the seminar-workshop Antropología de las Sensorialidades, Corporeidades y Performatividades, particularly during the pandemic and the social uprising that took place in Colombia in 2021. The second concerns the collaborative writing process with Laura Quintana that resulted in Esos afectos voraces, una correspondencia (2022). The third is the collective project Correspondencias Mutantes, developed during the pandemic and later continued in the book Enlaces vitales. Despite their differences, these experiences share a fundamental question: how can making, care, and correspondence become ways of knowing grounded in bodies, materials, and relations? The text maintains that these practices make it possible to move beyond a conception of knowledge based primarily on distance, representation, and productivity, proposing instead embodied, affective, and material forms of research and creation. Everyday activities such as writing, teaching, cooking, walking, observing, touching, exchanging images, and listening can become ways of thinking and producing knowledge. Making, then, is understood not as something that follows thought, but as a way of thinking in itself; care is presented as a necessary condition for building the common; and correspondence becomes a practice of attention, reciprocity, and transformation. Finally, the text proposes that creating and conducting research entail establishing relations among bodies, materials, territories, memories, and other beings.

RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: This is a cross-sectional observational study. Children's weight, height, blood pressure, serum levels of total cholesterol, triglycerides, HDL cholesterol, LDL cholesterol and non-HDL cholesterol were objectively measured from participants. Statistical analysis was performed using the ANOVA technique for parametric data and the Kruskal-Wallis test for nonparametric data. Study was conducted on 157 children aged 7-9 from two educational institutions located in low-income areas in Bogotá, Colombia. Weight excess (overweight and obesity) was observed in 46 subjects, of which 97.8% had a high or very high waist circumference. The lipid profile was altered in 45.2% of the subjects; 22.3% presented high levels of triglycerides. Metabolic syndrome was identified in 32.6% of the subjects with excess weight, thus being the most frequent component of high or very high waist circumference. Finally this study confirmed the high prevalence of malnutrition by excess weightand, also excess weight associated with high triglyceride and low HDL levels. The results of this study suggest the need for early and thorough interventions aimed at improving the lifestyles and quality of life of children.

RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: Abstract Protected areas (PAs) are central to Target 3 of the Kunming–Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, which calls for ecologically well-connected systems, yet progress is tracked with indicators of connectivity state rather than of what protection achieved. We evaluated whether PAs in Colombia maintained multispecies functional connectivity relative to unprotected counterfactuals from 2000 to 2022 and whether the magnitude of their effects reflected the pressure they faced. We grouped 181 bird and mammal species into 12 emergent functional groups (EFGs) based on movement traits and exposure to human modification, modeled their connectivity with omnidirectional circuit theory, and matched protected and unprotected pixels with propensity scores within 6 regional subsystems. For 135 PAs, we estimated effects on standardized connectivity change (ΔZ) and on avoided critical loss (connected pixels that became impeded) and classified PAs by avoided loss relative to control loss. Connectivity changed more favorably in PAs than in controls (median ΔZ effect 0.87, 95% CI 0.36–1.60); 72.6% of PAs had positive effects, which were significant in 4 of 6 regions. Protected areas avoided 1.51 percentage points (pp) of critical loss nationally, and avoided loss was positive in all 12 EFGs and significant in 8. However, the presence of an effect overstated its contribution: only 55% of PAs avoided more than 1 pp, and 30% lost more than their controls. Effectiveness increased with pressure, from 39% of PAs under low pressure to 75% under high pressure, where sustainable-use areas accounted for 29 of the 33 effective PAs. Small PAs contained most of the loss expected without protection (median 70%), and regional and national PAs performed alike under similar pressure. Measuring avoided loss relative to pressure shows where protection secures connectivity and where governance must improve, and offers a replicable indicator for the well-connected component of Target 3.

AUTORES: Óscar Humberto Alvarado-Sanabria; Javier Giovanni Álvarez-Herrera; Luz Marina Melgarejo
INSTITUCIONES_COLABORADORAS: Universidad Nacional de Colombia, Universidad Pedagógica y Tecnológica de Colombia
RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: Drought limits pea (Pisum sativum L.) productivity by reducing growth, photosynthesis, and reproductive success, yet comparative field data across contrasting canopy morphologies are scarce. This study evaluated five pea varieties—Alejandrita (short-climbing), San Isidro and Santa Isabel (tall-climbing), and two afila varieties (Afila, Rizada)—grown under plastic crop covers and subjected to terminal drought (irrigation withheld from flowering) or a fully irrigated control. This study measured photosynthetic variables, including gas exchange and chlorophyll fluorescence; predawn and midday leaf water potential; dry mass and yield components; and calculated intrinsic and irrigation water-use efficiencies. Terminal drought reduced canopy biomass and yield in all varieties, with stronger canopy-level effects than branch-level effects. Varietal responses diverged: Afila and San Isidro maintained higher intrinsic water-use efficiency and biomass yield and exhibited conservative reductions in CO2 assimilation; by contrast, Santa Isabel and Alejandrita showed earlier declines in leaf water potential and greater susceptibility to yield loss. Results indicate that drought tolerance was not determined solely by variety type; rather, leaf-level intrinsic water-use efficiency, the timing of water-potential decline, and reproductive resilience underpin varietal differences. These traits are promising targets for breeding, and, based on these results, afila varieties and San Isidro showed promising performance and merit further evaluation in multi-environment trials.

RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: El objetivo fue evaluar las edades de corte del pasto INIAP 811 sobre la composición química y la digestibilidad in vitro. Los tratamientos fueron: T1: 30 días; T2: 40 días y T3: 50 días de corte, con cinco repeticiones. Se utilizó un diseño completamente al azar (DCA). Se evaluó: materia seca (MS), materia orgánica (MO), proteína cruda (PC), fibra detergente neutra (FDN) y fibra detergente ácida (FDA). Para la digestibilidad in vitro de la materia seca (DIVMS), materia orgánica (DIVMO), fibra detergente neutra (DIVFDN) y fibra detergente ácida (DIVFDA). La MS y MO presentaron diferencias (p<0,05) registrando el tratamiento T3 (19,20 y 84,20%), así mismo, la PC, FDN y FDA la reportó el tratamiento T1 (12,26; 57,59 y 28,76%) . La mayor digestibilidad in vitro la reportó el T1 para la DIVMS, DIVMO, DIVFDN y DIVFDA (59,27; 53,37; 55,68 y 28,29%). La edad de corte del pasto influye en la composición química y su digestibilidad in vitro de los nutrientes. El siguiente objetivo fue evaluar el comportamiento productivo de bovinos Brahman x criollo, alimentados con el pasto INIAP 811 (Pennisetum) a los 30 días de edad durante la época lluviosa. Los tratamientos evaluados fueron: T1 (Machos castrados y hembras); T2 (Hembras); T3 (Machos enteros); T4 (Machos enteros y hembras), se utilizó un diseño completamente al azar (DCA), con 4 tratamientos y 4 repeticiones se utilizaron 16 bovinos no sexados de raza Brahman x criollo de 18 meses de edad. En las variables ganancia de peso y ganancia de peso diaria, el tratamiento T2 registró los mayores valores con 56 kg y 0,65 kg/día respectivamente. La relación beneficio/costo, el mayor valor fue el T2 con una rentabilidad de 46,66 %, seguido del tratamiento T4 con 43,42 % y el tratamiento con la rentabilidad más baja fue el T3 con 33,93 %.

INSTITUCIONES_COLABORADORAS: Universidad Nacional de Colombia, Washington State University, Oregon State University, Municipality of Medellín
RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: En este artículo se examina cómo la composición de la biomasa agroindustrial y las condiciones de pirólisis determinan la estructura molecular y el desempeño funcional del biochar desde una perspectiva de ingeniería de materiales. En el contexto colombiano y latinoamericano, la valorización descentralizada de residuos agrícolas y forestales (cascarilla de arroz, bagazo de caña, podas urbanas, residuos de palma y pulpa de café) representa una vía estratégica para la transición energética y la economía circular, en línea con los objetivos de desarrollo sostenible y el enfoque One Health. Se describen los procesos termoquímicos (torrefacción, pirólisis lenta y rápida y gasificación) y las rutas biológicas complementarias y se analizan los mecanismos que rigen la formación del biochar: despolimerización, fragmentación, condensación aromática y desarrollo de defectos estructurales. A partir de estos fundamentos, se construye una matriz que vincula las principales aplicaciones del biochar —secuestro de carbono, mejoramiento de suelos, catálisis heterogénea, adsorción de contaminantes y almacenamiento electroquímico de energía— con las características estructurales y las condiciones de síntesis que las favorecen. Se concluye que el biochar debe entenderse como un material diseñado, y no como un subproducto indiferenciado de la pirólisis, y se propone la ingeniería de biochar como marco para orientar su desarrollo hacia aplicaciones de alto valor agregado.

RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: As income inequality rises, cities do not merely become less equal in aggregate; they also sort residents into increasingly separate neighborhoods, a spatial process known as socioeconomic segregation. Building on a companion study that documented the luxury effect in Bogotá using cadastral land value (Mutis & Armenteras, 2026), this analysis asks a distinct question: does the city's institutionalized stratification system—the official six-tier "estratos" that determine utility subsidies, social stigma, and municipal investment—have an ecological signature of its own? We analyzed 118,447 eBird records (2010–2024) covering 258 species, spatially joined to cadastral strata. The three highest strata (4–6), occupying only 26.4% of the city's urban area, accounted for 52.3% of all bird occurrences, while the three lowest strata (1–3), covering 73.6% of the area, accounted for 47.7%. Species-level analyses revealed heterogeneity: habitat generalists occurred across all strata, wetland species clustered in strata 3–4, and forest specialists concentrated in stratum 6, coinciding with the Eastern Hills. A complementary analysis of the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) across 5,315 urban parks showed vegetation cover rising steadily from lower to higher strata (Tukey post-hoc, p < 0.05), positively correlating with bird richness (β = 72.7, p < 0.001). Together with the companion land-value analysis, these results suggest that in Bogotá the boundaries separating human social worlds also partition its avian communities and the vegetation that sustains them, with direct implications for equitable green-infrastructure planning in highly segregated cities of the Global South.

AUTORES: Andrés M. Gómez-Palacio; Johana Marín-Suarez; Laura Beltran-Rodriguez; Marcela Gómez; Weimar Briñez-Zabaleta; Abelgie Sanchez; Luz Helena Patiño; Sandra Uribe-Soto; Juan David Ramírez

RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: Aedes aegypti is the primary urban vector of major human arboviruses worldwide, yet the spatial genetic structure and demographic history of Colombian populations remain incompletely understood. Here, we analyzed mitochondrial cytochrome c oxidase subunit I (COX1) sequences from Colombian populations sampled across a broad geographic and temporal range to evaluate genetic diversity, haplotype distribution, spatial-temporal structure, and mitochondrial demographic history. The dataset combined publicly available COX1 records with 394 newly generated sequences from Colombian specimens, yielding 717 entries from the Caribbean, Andean, Orinoco, and Amazonian regions of Colombia, and was analyzed using population genetic, ordination, constrained spatial, and demographic inference approaches. Colombian COX1 diversity was mainly structured into two broad mitochondrial genetic clusters rather than by sampling locality, department, or collection year, suggesting the persistence of maternal lineages together with spatial mixing likely influenced by human-mediated dispersal and urban adaptation. Human population density and built-up intensity partially explained mitochondrial genetic structure, but this association varied through time, indicating that urbanization interacts with regional demographic heterogeneity and local habitat configuration. Demographic history analyses suggested temporal variation in mitochondrial effective population size, including an older increase followed by reduction and relative stabilization toward recent generations, rather than continuous demographic expansion. Climate-associated analyses further suggested that temperature, particularly minimum temperature, may contribute to mitochondrial demographic variation, although this relationship should be interpreted as correlative. Overall, Colombian Ae. aegypti populations appear to be shaped by historical maternal-lineage structure, urbanization-associated spatial heterogeneity, eco-regional demographic variation, and climatic context. This country-scale mitochondrial baseline can help prioritize regions for genomic, entomological, and epidemiological surveillance and guide future investigations of mosquito dispersal and population connectivity relevant to vector management in Colombia.

RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: Abstract The fragmentation of habitats in the Colombian biogeographical Choco threatens endemic species of high value such as the Vanilla rivasii orchid. To safeguard its ecological and biotechnological potential, it is crucial to develop specific in vitro propagation methods. This study established for the first time an asymbiotic germination and micropropagation protocol for this species. Germination was evaluated in 50% Murashige and Skoog medium (MS) supplemented with 0.02 mg L⁻ 1 1-naphthaleneacetic acid, 0.04 and 0.7 mg L⁻ 1 6-benzylaminopurine, 0.05 and 0.5 mg L⁻ 1 gibberellic acid, and 0.05 mg L⁻ 1 indole-3-butyric acid, using seeds at three phenological stages of the pod (immature, intermediate, mature). For micropropagation, nodal segments of different sizes were grown (small: 1.25 to1.56 cm; medium: 1.57 to 1.70 cm; large: 1.71 to1.90 cm). Only one of the bioregulatory combinations induced germination (0.02 mg L⁻ 1 1-naphthaleneacetic acid, 0.04 mg L⁻ 1 6-benzylaminopurine, and 0.05 mg L⁻ 1 gibberellic acid). The phenological stage of the pod was a determining factor. The seeds of pods at the intermediate stage showed an increase in germination (33%), significantly higher than those of green pods (16%) and mature pods (4%). In the multiplication phase, large explants showed the longest shoot length (2.25 cm at 30 d) and rhizogenesis (81% rooting), while small explants had the highest cumulative growth rate (133%). In conclusion, the study identifies an optimal phenological window for the germination of V. rivasii and demonstrates that the size of the explant defines divergent development trajectories. These findings offer novel and evidence-based criteria to optimize conservation and micropropagation protocols for this species.

RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: La concentración de la producción científica y de los recursos educativos digitales ha generado profundas desigualdades en el acceso al conocimiento. En Colombia, departamentos como Chocó enfrentan brechas estructurales en infraestructura tecnológica, cobertura educativa y oportunidades de participación en ecosistemas de innovación y aprendizaje. Este trabajo presenta una experiencia de diseño e implementación de un ecosistema territorial de aprendizaje basado en Recursos Educativos Abiertos (REA), Objetos Virtuales de Aprendizaje (OVA) y metodologías participativas desarrollada en comunidades afrodescendientes de Quibdó, capital del departamento del Chocó, en el Pacífico colombiano.

AUTORES: Estefanía Azuero; Jesús Riera; Emanuel David Santos-Suárez; Carlos Cecilio Góngora-Canul; Christian D. Cruz; Joaquin Gil
INSTITUCIONES_COLABORADORAS: Universidad Nacional de Colombia, Purdue University West Lafayette, Tecnológico Nacional de México
RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: Field-based RGB phenotyping is hampered by uncontrolled image acquisition (blur, variable illumination, occlusions, and complex backgrounds that bias severity estimates), while manual curation remains slow and unscalable. A reproducible automated workflow is therefore needed to handle multi-source imagery and support quantitative severity estimation across co-occurring phytosanitary conditions. We developed and validated a three-stage deep learning pipeline for maize tar spot, common rust, and fall armyworm damage, using multitemporal RGB images under field conditions from robotic and smartphone platforms across two countries and six sites, spanning growth stages V4-R6. The workflow proceeds stepwise: automated image quality assessment (IQA) to filter degraded images, leaf segmentation to isolate tissue from cluttered backgrounds, and lesion segmentation to quantify severity over the segmented leaf. Rather than a pre-selected model, we benchmarked multiple architectures per stage under identical partitions, reporting computational and environmental cost alongside accuracy. Xception matched expert curation (97.4% accuracy) while cutting screening time by up to 99.8%; U-Net++ with a ResNet34 encoder gave the most robust leaf delineation; and a hybrid U-Net–ResNet34–XGBoost model, fusing deep features with engineered descriptors, achieved the strongest lesion segmentation under severe class imbalance. End-to-end, the integrated pipeline reduced class-level MAE by 47.1% and RMSE by 54.9% versus unfiltered analysis, approached negligible bias, and lowered detection emissions by ~12%. This reproducible, resource-efficient framework moves field phenotyping beyond classification toward reliable severity quantification, and is potentially transferable to other crops and phytosanitary problems.

RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: Polydopamine nanoparticles (PDA NPs) have considerable potential for biomedical and adsorption applications, but their production still relies on high-purity reagents and costly analytical techniques, which may hinder their implementation at larger scales. This study investigated strategies to reduce PDA NP production and characterization costs while preserving their physicochemical and functional properties. Distilled low-cost (LC) ethanol (EtOH-LC) and 2-propanol (2-PrOH-LC) were evaluated as alternatives to their high-purity counterparts, while EtOH and NH 4 OH recovered from the reaction supernatant were reused over three consecutive synthesis cycles. The type of alcohol (ROH) used for polymerization had a greater influence on NP properties than its grade: replacing high-purity EtOH and 2-PrOH with their LC alternatives did not significantly affect particle size or Fe 3+ and Cu 2+ adsorption, whereas 2-PrOH produced smaller NPs with higher Fe 3+ adsorption capacity than EtOH. The use of LC ROH reduced the estimated production cost by approximately 36-41%. Furthermore, 72.9 ± 2% of EtOH and 42.1 ± 1% of NH 4 OH were recovered from the synthesis medium, and their reuse yielded PDA NPs with physicochemical properties comparable to those prepared using fresh reagents. Commercial UV-Vis colorimetric kits provided Fe 3+ and Cu 2+ adsorption values differing by less than 3% from those obtained by ICP-AES, supporting their potential use for routine assessment of metal adsorption as a functional quality-control parameter. Finally, substitution with LC alcohols preserved the intrinsic antineoplastic activity of PDA NPs against BT474 cells while maintaining lower cytotoxicity toward HS5 cells. Overall, the combined use of lower-cost reagents, recovery and reuse of synthesis components, and accessible analytical methods provided a practical approach to reducing PDA NP production and characterization costs without compromising their key physicochemical and functional properties.

RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: The Golondrinas archaeological site is in the Colombian inter-Andean Aburrá Valley hillslopes (2,000 m a.s.l). The initial archaeological assessment presented here included field observations, archaeological survey, soil chemistry, palynology, and micromorphological analyses in five locations, to identify a representative site. The complete pedostratigraphic sequence was analyzed to characterize depositional and post-depositional processes and to evaluate the effects of pedoturbation, pedogenesis, and anthropogenic features in relation to paleohydrological information. The archaeological record was assessed through a soil profile representative of the Golondrinas site (3,800 m2) described at microscale. The results provide a basis for testing hypotheses and proposing interpretations about past ecological conditions and historical land use dynamics at the study site. The findings and soil analyses suggest a history of land use that may have been associated with relatively high biological activity and high organic carbon content under hydromorphic conditions, as well as with alternating phases of agricultural activity and natural forest cover in the past. The study also identifies the presence of significant surface water flows and episodes of landslide activity associated with the site's geomorphological setting, which may have influenced both historical and contemporary land-use patterns.

RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: Food security remains a challenge in Colombian indigenous communities, particularly due to limited access to animal protein and reliance on external supplies. This study aimed to foster the social appropriation of knowledge through the participatory implementation of an aquaponic system at the Kaggaba Matshukumake Rural Ethno-educational Center, located in the Kogui Maruámake reserve in the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta. Employing a participatory action research approach, students, teachers, community leaders, and researchers collaborated on the system's design, construction, and commissioning. The system integrated fish-rearing tanks, grow beds, and a photovoltaic system to ensure energy autonomy. Red tilapia (Oreochromis spp.) and bocachico (Prochilodus magdalenae) were raised alongside crops such as chives, beans, maize, cassava, arracacha, tomatoes, and cilantro. Workshops and educational tools were also developed to strengthen local capacities and facilitate dialogue between scientific and traditional knowledge systems. The results demonstrated the system's technical, productive, and community viability. Tilapia reached an average weight of 357.6 g and a length of 24.6 cm, while bocachico specimens averaged 14.9 g and 10.5 cm. Powered by solar energy, the system enabled the simultaneous production of animal protein and vegetables to supplement school meals. Educational activities enhanced learning and the adoption of technologies for sustainable food production. In conclusion, participatory aquaponics represents a viable strategy for strengthening food security and sovereignty in indigenous communities by promoting technological autonomy, renewable energy use, and the integration of scientific and ancestral knowledge, with the potential for replication in similar territories.

RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: This concept paper reconstructs the public agrarian university as an institutional configuration of recognition and reads the rural–urban gap at the threshold of higher education as one material expression of it. The reconstruction runs from Hegel’s assignment of the agricultural estate to immediate ethical life, through the developmentalist reception of classical sociology, to Honneth’s spheres of recognition, Fraser’s institutionalized status hierarchies, and a Latin American rural sociology in which the peasant appears as knowledge-producer; it is anchored by an abductive diagnosis of published indicators. Across six Latin American countries with heterogeneous redistributive regimes, the rural–urban gap in secondary completion narrowed between 2010 and 2022, while the residential attendance gap at ages 20–24, an imperfect proxy for tertiary participation, converged more slowly in five of the six and not at all in three; the difference between the two trends is significant in every country except Chile. In Colombia, rural secondary completion rose by 20.6 percentage points while rural attendance at these ages rose by less than one. The patterns do not identify a causal mechanism; they delimit resource-based, Bourdieusian, capabilities, selection-based, and compositional accounts rather than refute them, and the paper states what would disconfirm its diagnosis. Three contributions follow. First, the non-reporting of rural origin in the higher education information systems is argued to be institutional misrecognition rather than a resource constraint: the same state records peasant self-identification in four statistical operations, the enrolment file records forty-one attributes of the student, and none is territorial origin, and the omission forecloses accountability for inequalities in admission, persistence, and graduation. Second, epistemic reciprocity is offered as the criterion of curricular reform. Third, the framework identifies reform sites and observable success criteria that resource-based accounts do not reach.

RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: Quarry sludge (QS), a residue generated by the washing operations during the manufacture of aggregate materials used for mortar and concrete, is considered a local environmental threat for air, water, and different ecosystems. This study aimed to assess the feasibility of using the alkali activation of fly ash (FA) with a potassium hydroxide solution to stabilize the residue as an environmentally friendly solution to elaborate compressed earth blocks (CEBs). QS–FA systems were characterized by using Proctor compaction, unconfined compressive strength (UCS), scanning electron microscopy/energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy, X-ray diffraction, and a computational analysis model. The results showed that this approach is an alternative for the elaboration of CEBs with estimated strength levels potentially compatible with Type 5 classification (up to 8 MPa compressive strength). While increasing the fly ash content, the K2O/Al2O3 molar ratio achieved values between 0.5 and 1.5, developing the best UCS with 40 °C curing temperature due to the formation of a K-Al-Si-rich reaction product (K-A-S-H-type).

RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: Despite the importance of the Galápagos archipelago as a key site for the study of biodiversity and evolution, significant components of its invertebrate biodiversity, particularly Hymenoptera, remain insufficiently documented. Occurrence records of Hymenoptera from 1959-2025 were combined from structured surveys of non-formicid Hymenoptera, long-term ant sampling, museum collections, literature, and online sources to assess the richness, distribution, and species composition of hymenopterans across the archipelago. Based on 21,364 records, 524 species/morphospecies, including 137 species, one subspecies, and 386 morphospecies are documented. These records include 20 newly recorded species and 134 newly recorded genera for Galápagos, representing 11 previously unrecorded families. These records substantially increase previous estimates, with the greatest additions observed in Chalcidoidea and Ichneumonoidea. Species accumulation curves and incidence-based richness estimators (Bootstrap = 595.47, Jackknife 1 = 673.38, Chao2 = 658.26) indicate that additional species/morphospecies may remain undocumented. Species/morphospecies richness was positively associated with island area after accounting for sampling effort. Species composition showed partial similarity among some islands and overlap among the littoral, dry, and transition zones; the humid zone contained the highest proportion of unique species/morphospecies. A considerable proportion of the named species were classified as introduced. Overall, this study establishes an updated baseline for future Hymenoptera research in Galápagos and provides a framework for evaluating biogeographic patterns in oceanic island systems.

RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: Introduction: Dental mesowear and microwear analyses provide complementary proxies for reconstructing herbivore feeding ecology at different temporal scales. While mesowear reflects long-term dietary abrasion, microwear captures short-term feeding behavior, allowing evaluation of dietary stability and variability in seasonally dynamic tropical environments. Objectives: To assess short- and long-term dietary patterns in two Neotropical cervids, the white-tailed deer (Odocoileus virginianus) and the Central American red brocket deer (Mazama temama), and to evaluate the ecological significance of microwear variability in relation to habitat, seasonality, and foraging behavior. Methods: Dental mesowear and low magnification microwear analyses were conducted on lower molars of modern cervid specimens from Costa Rica. Microwear variables, including pits, scratches, and scratch texture, were recorded within standardized enamel areas. Scratch variability was assessed using standard deviation and coefficient of variation, and results were interpreted through comparative and descriptive approaches. Results: Odocoileus virginianus exhibited moderate mesowear values combined with low microwear dispersion, indicating a stable feeding strategy. In contrast, M. temama showed greater variability in microwear features, particularly in scratch counts, showing a broader diet. Conclusions: Tropical cervids may maintain consistent long-term feeding strategies while exhibiting variable short-term dietary responses driven by ecological context and resource availability. Integrating mesowear, microwear, and microwear variability provides a robust framework for interpreting cervid feeding ecology in both modern and archaeological contexts, with implications for future comparative studies across tropical environments.

RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: Abstract Quantifying foliar disease severity accurately and reproducibly remains a fundamental challenge in plant pathology, as traditional visual assessment is inherently subjective and prone to rater variability. Although computer vision has enabled automated disease detection, validated end-to-end frameworks that integrate reference generation, model training, and field-deployable percent severity estimation are lacking. Here, we developed and validated a computer vision pipeline for quantifying powdery mildew ( Oidium spp.) severity in pea ( Pisum sativum ) using smartphone-acquired images under field conditions, with tomato ( Solanum lycopersicum ) powdery mildew serving as a cross-species validation system. A semi-automated multichannel segmentation approach generated continuous percent severity estimates as reproducible training references. Among evaluated deep learning architectures, a YOLO-based model was selected for its superior balance of predictive accuracy, computational efficiency, and deployment flexibility and was integrated into PowderyComputerVision, a purpose-built web application enabling real-time inference. Under field conditions, the automated system showed substantially higher agreement with reference severity values than trained human raters (concordance correlation coefficient (CCC), 0.952 vs. 0.513). A linear mixed-effects model revealed that human evaluators produced absolute estimation errors 280.96 times greater than the automated system ( p < 0.0001; 95% CI 120.34–655.91). Performance remained robust across variable lighting conditions, imaging angles, and plant structures, supporting applicability beyond controlled settings. The proposed four-stage pipeline comprising image capture, host and disease classification via YOLOv11m-cls, leaf localization via YOLOv11n-seg, and lesion quantification via multichannel segmentation offers a scalable, objective, and reproducible framework for continuous field-based disease severity estimation.

RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: Cocoa (Theobroma cacao L.) is considered one of the most important crops in Colombia; however, nutritional disorders have been associated with reduced yields. The objective of this study was to establish a Diagnosis and Recommendation Integrated System (DRIS) standard for K+, Ca2+, Mg2+, and S2+. Data were obtained from an experimental cocoa plantation located in the Department of Cauca, Colombia. A statistical analysis of 1440 interactions among foliar nutrients was performed based on means, variances, coefficients of variation, and standard deviation. The cocoa clones evaluated were CCN-51 (self-compatible) and ICS-39 (self-incompatible). Based on the highest variance values, 15 nutrient relationships were selected as DRIS standards for assessing the nutritional status of cocoa in Colombia. These relationships were identified as NP, NK, NCa, NMg, NS, KP, KCa, KMg, KS, CaP, CaMg, CaS, MgS, MgP, and SP. The nutrient indices revealed deficiencies in the order K > N > Ca > Mg and excesses in the order S > P for CCN-51. In contrast, ICS-39 showed deficiencies in the order K > Ca and excesses in the order P > Mg > N > S.

RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: This article examines three Shakespearean adaptations from the BabyLit series—Romeo & Juliet: A Counting Primer, Macbeth: A Potions Primer, and A Midsummer Night’s Dream: A Fairies Primer—to explore how the primer genre enables the adaptation of canonical drama for pre-literate infants. Drawing on theories of dual address in children’s literature and studies of cultural capital, the article argues that primers function as formal mechanisms through which BabyLit sustains a double promise: delivering sensory and educational experience to infants while signalling cultural distinction to adult purchasers. The analysis proceeds in two stages. First, it examines the paratexts (e.g., taglines, branding, marketing copy) through which BabyLit constructs its dual audience within the early childhood publishing market. Second, through close readings of three primers, it demonstrates how each subgenre reorganises Shakespeare’s texts differently: Romeo & Juliet fragments tragedy through enumeration; Macbeth reframes witchcraft as botanical cataloguing; A Midsummer Night’s Dream transforms erotic chaos into lullaby rhythm. These formal strategies reveal how genre choice determines not merely what content is adapted but what Shakespeare can become when addressed to readers aged 0–3, exposing the intersection of adaptation, pedagogy, and cultural capital in contemporary children’s literature.

RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: Computer-assisted synthesis planning (CASP) software allows experimentalists to streamline setups and reduce unsuccessful experiments. CASP has a long history, yet remains an active research area. Although various tools have been developed and published, few have remained publicly available and continue to be supported. Those available at no-cost typically operate on generalized global databases, ignoring domain-or laboratory-specific constraints. Here, we present LAGER, a graph-grammar-based retrosynthesis engine built on the Double Pushout (DPO) formalism of the MØD framework. Retrosynthetic pathways are resolved by a state-based A∗ search with a weighted evaluation function. The path cost, g(n), penalizes pathway length and chemoselectivity risks from competing side reactions, whereas the heuristic h(n) estimates chemical distance to available reactants using fragment-based synthetic accessibility score (SAscore) to prioritize structurally simpler precursors and limit search-space expansion. LAGER is designed to accelerate synthesis planning for subsequent generations of a specific compound series by leveraging synthetic knowledge from previous generations. Its reaction library therefore comprises well-established reactions routinely used within a particular laboratory alongside readily available starting materials. We evaluate LAGER on a benchmark of 109 investigated inhibitors of elastase B (LasB), a key virulence factor of the Gram-negative bacterium Pseudomonas aeruginosa. With appropriate heuristic weighting, LAGER recovers the experimentally used pathway among Top-3 proposed pathways for up to 81% of targets. Importantly, deviation from the reported route did not imply chemical infeasibility: at least one chemically valid pathway was identified within the Top-3 candidates for 98% of targets. However, our results indicate limitations of SAscore as a chemical distance metric for targeted retrosynthesis, highlighting the need for more robust, computationally efficient alternatives. Comparison with AiZynthFinder using identical starting materials further demonstrated the importance of laboratory-specific reaction knowledge, as general reactiontemplate sets rarely reproduced the complete literature route for the investigated compounds and often included only a subset of the key transformations in the proposed pathways. Scientific Contribution. This work demonstrates the value of incorporating laboratory-specific reaction knowledge into automated retrosynthetic planning. Unlike general-purpose approaches, LAGER explicitly encodes domain-specific transformations within an interpretable graph-grammar-based search framework, providing a customizable approach for synthesis planning within a defined chemical space.

RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: This paper addresses the problem of constraint violations in reinforcement learning (RL) for power-system operation, with application to steady-state optimal-power-flow tasks. While RL-based controllers can achieve competitive reward performance, they may produce actions that violate operational constraints, limiting their practical applicability in steady-state optimal-power-flow (OPF) tasks. We investigate a deployment-time safety framework in which a continuous constraint-violation surrogate is learned directly from state–action–violation samples generated by the power-system simulator. Once the nominal Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) policy has been trained, it remains fixed, and candidate actions are corrected by minimizing their deviation from the original policy output while penalizing the violation predicted by the learned surrogate. The correction is performed directly over the nonlinear surrogate using projected gradient descent, and linear and quadratic penalty formulations are empirically compared. The framework is evaluated on two complementary OPF-Gym benchmarks, EcoDispatch and MaxRenewables, which differ in their optimization objectives, network topologies, actuator compositions, and control dimensionalities. Large-scale out-of-sample simulations show substantial reductions in the frequency and severity of constraint violations relative to nominal SAC, Lagrangian-penalty SAC, Recovery RL, and linearized correction baselines; across both benchmarks, the exact-gradient variants substantially reduce physical constraint violations relative to nominal SAC and the linearized correction strategies. In EcoDispatch, these feasibility improvements are additionally achieved while maintaining reward performance close to the underlying SAC controller. RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: Companies are under increasing social pressure to promote sustainable development while remaining competitive — a challenge that is closely linked to organizational culture and lean practices. To contribute to solving this problem, this study analyzed the relationship between national culture, lean practices and corporate sustainability in large and medium-sized companies in two Latin American emerging economies. To this end, a Likert-scale survey was administered to 313 business executives in Bogotá (Colombia) and Quito (Ecuador). The data were analyzed using structural equation modelling. The results revealed a moderately positive correlation between lean practices and corporate sustainability, but an insignificant correlation between national culture and corporate sustainability. This finding contrasts with previous research on this relationship in developed economies, where corporate commitment to social, cultural, and environmental issues has become a central strategy for improving corporate sustainability and competitiveness. In this regard, the study provides empirical evidence and a theoretical review to help academics, business leaders and government officials responsible for public policy related to business activity in emerging economies gain a better understanding of sociocultural management and lean practices. This will facilitate effective decision-making aimed at fostering competitive and sustainable businesses in increasingly demanding environments.

RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: The integration of distributed energy resources (DERs) into active distribution networks (ADNs) aggravates existing observability limitations, demanding advanced measurement infrastructure beyond traditional SCADA systems. Micro-phasor measurement units (μPMUs) provide synchronized, high-resolution measurements at sampling rates between 30 and 120 samples per second. However, their high cost—approximately 22 times that of advanced metering infrastructure (AMI) devices—limits large-scale deployment. This paper formulates a mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) model for the Joint Placement of μPMUs and AMI meters that minimizes capital expenditure (CAPEX) while guaranteeing complete topological observability, DER coverage, and channel constraints. RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: Cobalt ferrite (CoFe2O4) is a multifunctional spinel oxide whose structural, optical, and magnetic properties are strongly influenced by the synthesis route and thermal treatment. Establishing the relationship between the synthesis conditions and the resulting structural, compositional, optical, and magnetic characteristics is essential for assessing the properties of the material obtained by sol-gel auto-combustion. Here, we synthesized CoFe2O4 powder by a urea-assisted sol-gel auto-combustion route and systematically characterized it to determine its crystal structure, chemical composition, optical response, and magnetic behavior. The precursors were dissolved in distilled water and heated progressively to 420 °C to promote spontaneous combustion; the resulting powder was subsequently calcined at 700 °C for 3 h. X-ray diffraction followed by Rietveld refinement confirmed the formation of a single-phase cubic inverse-spinel structure with space group Fd-3m and a lattice parameter of 8.3801 Å. SEM observations revealed fine, predominantly irregular to sub-spherical particles with moderate agglomeration; particle dimensions were estimated to be on the order of 100 nm, while EDS analysis showed a composition close to the nominal CoFe2O4 stoichiometry. Diffuse-reflectance measurements and Kubelka–Munk analysis yielded a direct optical band gap of 1.45 ± 0.05 eV. Room-temperature magnetization measurements up to 15 kOe revealed ferrimagnetic behavior, with a magnetization approaching 50 emu g⁻¹ at the maximum applied field. These results establish the structural, compositional, optical, and magnetic characteristics of CoFe2O4 produced by the selected sol-gel auto-combustion route and provide a basis for further studies of its functional properties.

RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: The southern house mosquito Culex quinquefasciatus is a major disease vector for multiple arboviruses, including West Nile virus and St. Louis encephalitis virus. Insecticides are widely used to control Cx. quinquefasciatus populations, but resistant mosquitoes have emerged in numerous locations across the globe, including the United States. Much progress has been made in recent years in identifying insecticide resistance (IR) mutations in various pest species. In most species, these studies have focused primarily on SNPs as they are readily detectable. However, several genomic structural variants (SVs) have been experimentally shown to impact IR in Drosophila melanogaster, and structural variation has been observed in natural populations of vector species at a few genes that may be relevant to IR (e.g., cytochrome P450s). Because most population genomic data are derived from short sequencing reads, which fail to detect a large fraction of SVs, the contribution of structural variants to the evolution of IR and other adaptations in vector species is likely to be underestimated in the absence of long-read sequencing data. Here, we present the first genome-wide assessment of structural variants in Cx. quinquefasciatus from wild populations in Puerto Rico and Zambia using PacBio long-read sequencing. We constructed high-quality genome assemblies for each and found a total of 259,046 SVs which consisted predominantly of insertions and deletions. We found that 154,071 of these variants contained or overlapped genes. Of these SVs, 5,225 intersected IR genes and 56 of these were predicted to result in changes to downstream protein function. Several SVs predicted to severely impact protein-coding genes also coincided with signatures of selective sweeps, highlighting their possible role as targets of selection. Many of these variants would have gone undetected using short-read approaches, underscoring the importance of long-read sequencing for comprehensive population genetic analyses of adaptation to pesticides and other strong selective pressures, not only in insects but across the tree of life.

RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: The agricultural sector is an essential pillar for economic development and global food security. However, it faces challenges that compromise its viability, such as climate change, migration, and productivity variability. Colombia is among the main producing countries of fine and aromatic cocoa, and the department of Santander is the main producer of cocoa in the country; however, its production and commercialisation are affected by multiple factors, such as low access to competitive markets, a lack of infrastructure, and a low level of incorporation of technologies. In this study, the efficiency of cocoa on 500 farms located in five municipalities, Santander and Norte de Santander, Colombia, was analysed using a two-stage method with bootstrapped DEA and truncated regression. The results revealed 68.4% average technical efficiency and 21.5% scale efficiency. Efficiency is affected by technological limitations, training, and market factors. In addition, it was shown that gender gaps persist, with female producers showing significantly lower scale efficiency, suggesting structural barriers in access to productive resources, financing, and technical assistance, as well as a worrying lack of generational change.

RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: Potato yellow vein virus (PYVV; Crinivirus flavisolani) is a major limiting virus in potato production in Colombia and other South American countries. This virus is transmitted by both seed tubers and the whitefly Trialeurodes vaporariorum. While PYVV has also been reported in naranjilla, cape gooseberry, and tomato, its epidemiology in these solanaceous species remains poorly understood. Unlike potatoes, these crops are propagated by sexual seeds and are commercially distributed as seedlings. This study evaluated the presence of PYVV in tomato crops from various departments in Colombia using RT-qPCR with different tissues including leaves, fruit pericarp, seeds, and seedling shoots. The genomic identity of the virus was confirmed through high-throughput sequencing (HTS) of leaf samples from the Chonto tomato variety. A seed-to-seedling transmission assay was also conducted using surface-disinfected seeds cultured in vitro on MS medium. The virus was detected in 75% of fruit samples, 35% of leaf samples, and 40% of seedling shoot samples, but only in 10% of non-commercial seeds and none of the commercial seeds. HTS enabled assembly of the nearly complete viral genome with high sequencing depth. The in vitro assay indicated that PYVV has a low-frequency seed-to-seedling transmission in tomato, suggesting that disease management strategies should prioritize control of the whitefly vectors.

RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: BACKGROUND: The valorization of citrus by-products, especially peels and fibrous fractions, has gained increasing attention due to their high bioactive compound content and the need to mitigate associated environmental impacts. Spray drying is widely applied to produce stable fruit powder; however, most studies on spray-dried Tahiti lime (Citrus latifolia Tanaka) focus on juice or essential oil fractions, overlooking the whole fruit matrix. This study optimized formulation and spray-drying conditions to produce a powder from whole Tahiti lime and evaluated its physicochemical properties. RESULTS: Response surface methodology identified optimal process conditions, yielding Tahiti lime powder with a low moisture content (~3.6%) and water activity (~0.25), suggesting favorable storage stability. The powder exhibited good solubility (~84%), with minor limitations attributed to the insoluble constituents of the native matrix. The optimized product retained a relevant bioactive compound content, with mean total phenolic and flavonoid contents of approximately 522 mg gallic acid equivalents and 148 mg quercetin equivalents per 100 g dry basis, respectively. The antioxidant activity was preserved, as indicated by the ABTS and DPPH values of approximately 138 and 267 mg Trolox equivalents per 100 g dry basis, respectively. CONCLUSION: Spray drying is an effective approach for transforming whole Tahiti lime into a stable powder and preserving key physicochemical and antioxidant attributes. These findings support the sustainable valorization of citrus by-products and highlight the potential of whole-fruit spray-dried powders as ingredients in food and related industries. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.

RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: We present a phytosociological classification of the submerged, free-floating, and rooted floating-leaved aquatic vegetation of the hydric series in the Colombian Caribbean, based on its floristic composition and structural aspects. The vegetation surveys were conducted during both the rainy season (high water levels) and the dry season (low water levels); electrical conductivity and pH were also measured. The most diverse group was rooted floating-leaved vegetation, specifically the class Pontederio azureae-Paspaletea repentis, which included two orders, three alliances, and 34 associations. In the free-floating group, the classes Lemnetea minoris and Pistio stratiotis-Pontederietea crassipedis were identified with two orders, two alliances, and twelve associations, and in submerged vegetation, the class Cabombo-Nymphaeetea was found with one order, two alliances, and five associations. One class, two orders, five alliances, and 30 associations are newly described syntaxa. Species richness, community structure, and changes associated with the filling and drawdown cycle of the wetlands are consistent with the patterns reported for wetland environments of Central and South America and the Caribbean. The extent (cover) of the floating and rooted floating-leaved groups was greater during periods of rising waters, when they covered almost the entire water surface of the wetlands. In general, the floristic composition and structural aspects of the submerged, free-floating, and rooted floating-leaved vegetation in the Caribbean resemble those of similar environments in Central America, Mexico, the Antilles, and sectors of the Brazilian Pantanal, the Chaco, and the “savannas” of Bolivia and Paraguay.

RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: Coral reefs are crucial habitats for many fish species because they serve as feeding and shelter sites. However, due to their sensitivity to environmental changes, reef degradation has led to a drastic decline in fish and reef assemblages, which has also been reflected in associated economic activities. The loss of branching corals Acropora palmata and A. cervicornis has reached up to 90% in the Colombian Caribbean, resulting in a reduction in the abundance and diversity of associated fish populations. During two time periods (2011–2012 and 2023–2024) across the Colombian Caribbean, fish associated with Acropora formations were evaluated in relation to patch size and health status of these coral species. The best conserved patches of A. palmata were found in the Tayrona National Natural Park (TNNP) and of A. cervicornis in the reefs of the Urabá Gulf. A total of 113 fish species from 34 families were associated with A. palmata , with the most represented families being Labridae, Haemulidae, Pomacentridae, and Serranidae. Acanthurus coeruleus, A. tractus, Chaetodon ocellatus, Haemulon flavolineatum, Scarus iseri , Sparisoma viride , Thalassoma bifasciatum, Abudefduf saxatilis , Microspathodon chrysurus , Stegastes adustus , and Canthigaster rostrata were the species common to all reef locations. In A. cervicornis formations, 78 species belonging to 25 families were recorded, with Labridae and Pomacentridae as the most abundant. Stegastes planifrons , Cephalopholis cruentata, and Hypoplectrus puella were the species common to all locations. The highest number of fish species was found in the TNNP (85 for A. palmata , 55 for A. cervicornis ). Although the status is critical throughout the Caribbean, further aggravated by the 2023–2024 bleaching event which caused A. palmata formations to practically disappear from two localities, this structural loss has not yet been reflected in the associated ichthyofauna. These results suggest that the fish assemblages linked to Acropora corals in the Colombian Caribbean remain relatively stable; however, it is unclear for how long they will persist.

RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: Bean rust, caused by Uromyces appendiculatus , is one of the most critical diseases affecting common bean ( Phaseolus vulgaris L.) worldwide. Similarly, common bacterial blight, caused by Xanthomonas fuscans subsp. fuscans (Xff) and Xanthomonas axonopodis pv. phaseoli (Xap), poses major threats to common bean production globally. While common bean exhibits limited natural resistance to these pathogens, tepary bean ( Phaseolus acutifolius A. Gray), a closely related species, has shown resistance to both rust and common bacterial blight. This study aimed to identify tepary beans resistant to rust and Xff, to pinpoint genomic regions controlling this resistance. Twenty-three tepary bean genotypes were inoculated with multiple rust races and Xff isolates. Several tepary genotypes exhibited immunity to eight rust races, and a few were also resistant to two isolates of Xff. An F 2 biparental tepary bean population was developed from one resistant and one susceptible genotype to map quantitative trait loci (QTLs) for resistance to these pathogens. The population was phenotyped by inoculating with two rust races and a mixture of two isolates of Xff. Genotyping by sequencing was employed to genotype the biparental population. A major QTL for the rust pathogen was identified on chromosome Pa10, and a major QTL for common bacterial blight fuscans was identified on chromosome Pa07. Neither of these QTLs have been previously reported in common bean, suggesting that tepary bean possesses different genes controlling the resistance to both pathogens. Both tepary genes should be considered for introgression into common bean through interspecific crossing.

RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: Postharvest processing modifies the composition and sensory characteristics of coffee, although global antioxidant assays may not reflect changes in individual metabolites. This study compared Washed, Natural, and Honey processes in Caturra coffee obtained from the same farm, lot, and harvest. The lot was divided into nine independent experimental units, with three replicates assigned to each process. Analytical determinations were subsequently performed in triplicate. Polyphenols, flavonoids, condensed tannins, four phenolic acids, and antioxidant responses determined using DPPH, ABTS, and ORAC assays were evaluated. Sensory profiles were established by consensus among three expert assessors. Honey coffee showed the highest total polyphenol content (3,136.35 mg GAE 100 g-1 d.s.) but lower concentrations of individual phenolic acids. Chlorogenic acid reached 46.9 mg 100 g-1 d.s. in Honey coffee and 316.5 mg 100 g-1 d.s. in Washed coffee; caffeic acid was not detected in Honey coffee but reached 388.2 mg 100 g-1 d.s. in Washed coffee. ORAC differed among the three processes, whereas ABTS was lower in Honey coffee than in Washed and Natural coffees. Washed coffee was balanced and pleasant; Natural coffee exhibited greater fragrance and wine-like notes; and Honey coffee showed higher acidity and sweet and citrus descriptors. Differences between global antioxidant assays and individual phenolic acids support the use of complementary analytical approaches. Under standardized fermentation and drying conditions, postharvest processing can alter the chemical and sensory profile of specialty coffees.

RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: Flash vacuum expansion is an emerging thermophysical technology that combines rapid fruit heating with instantaneous decompression in a vacuum chamber to obtain high-quality purees. To date, this technology has been mainly studied in batch systems, with limited evidence regarding its application in small and medium-scale agro-industries. This study evaluated the technical performance and techno-economic feasibility of a continuous flash vacuum expansion process for the production of Andean blackberry puree. A 2 × 2 factorial design was applied, testing two heating times (48 and 67 s) and two feed rates (4 and 6 kg·min⁻¹). Heat transfer was modeled using a transient conduction–convection approach with temperature-dependent properties. Product analyses included microbial inactivation, retention of cyanidins, ellagitannins, and ascorbic acid (UHPLC-DAD), as well as the evaluation of texture, color, and sensory attributes. The optimal condition (48 s, 6 kg·min⁻¹) achieved a 72% yield, a 7-log microbial reduction, and a 77% increase in cyanidin content compared with the untreated puree. Ellagitannins, ascorbic acid, and sensory attributes were preserved, confirming the high functional quality of the product. Economic projections over 15 years indicated a payback period of approximately two years and an internal rate of return of 93%, surpassing values commonly reported for conventional fruit-processing technologies. These results demonstrate, for the first time, that continuous flash vacuum expansion at industrial scale ensures microbial safety, enhances bioactive compound retention, and represents a technically and economically viable alternative for small and medium-scale agro-industries.
